subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography — Settlements
subtitle: Revision pack for settlement sites, functions, patterns, hierarchy and sustainability
description: A source-faithful KS3 geography pack covering why settlements develop, how they are classified, and how places can become more sustainable. It includes key terminology, applied recall, ordering tasks and reading comprehension based on the supplied study pack.

data.title: Why An Early Settlement Site Was Chosen
data.instruction: Put these ideas in a sensible order to show how a good settlement site could attract settlers.
items: A place near a river offers a reliable water supply.
Flat land makes farming, transport and building easier.
Fertile soil helps crops grow and supports food production.
People build homes using nearby materials such as wood or stone.
Trade and movement increase because the site has good transport links.

data.title: Settlement Hierarchy
data.instruction: Order these settlements from the smallest to the largest in the hierarchy.

data.title: Making A Settlement More Sustainable
data.instruction: Put these planning ideas in order from identifying a problem to improving life in the settlement.
items: Planners identify problems such as traffic, pollution or lack of green space.
They improve public transport, walking routes and cycle lanes.
They add greener housing features such as insulation and solar panels.
They protect or create parks, trees and wildlife habitats.
The settlement becomes cleaner, healthier and better prepared for the future.
